memory_candidates.content: Pattern: compute a cross-cutting invariant ONCE at a single canonical stage (the skill's postflight), then render it independently at every consumer surface via a three-branch, all-non-silent resolution: (1) use the field directly if the producing stage already wrote it, (2) compute a fallback from a lower-level primitive if the structured field is absent but the primitive is present, (3) print an explicit 'not evaluable' notice and fall through to ordinary rendering if neither is present -- never silently skip. This keeps detection single-sourced while letting rendering degrade gracefully across skill variants (e.g. a hard-mode variant that delegates to the same base stages) without any branch falling through to silence.

Technique for smoke-testing a deploy-root-guarded script (one sourcing deploy-root-guard.sh, which refuses to run outside a .claude/scripts/ or .opencode/scripts/ shaped tree) without touching the live deploy tree: build a scratch tree under the scratchpad directory with a .claude/scripts/ subdirectory, copy the target script plus every script it calls via SCRIPT_DIR-relative paths (grep for "$SCRIPT_DIR/*.sh" references to enumerate them), copy any required context/reference/*.json data files, and write a synthetic specs/state.json with fixture active_projects entries. This reproduces exactly the guard's structural check (two directories under a .claude or .opencode parent) while remaining fully isolated from the real repo state.

Confirmed recurring gotcha: deploy-headless.sh's picker sync tool excludes skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md and skill-orchestrate-hard/SKILL.md from its skills scan, so any source-store edit to these two files requires a direct-copy workaround (cp agent-system/extensions/core/skills/skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md .claude/skills/skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md) immediately after every deploy-headless.sh invocation, verified by diffing the copy against the source. This has now recurred across at least two tasks; a dedicated follow-up task to fix the sync tool itself is recommended rather than continuing to route around it.
